# A root-simplex incidence obstruction

## Statement and scope

Let `K` be any characteristic-zero field. On the 112 live E8 root lines,
let `ell(t)` be the pinned binary label and let

```
C = {c_h : c_h(t) = <r_t,h>, h in K^8},
w(q) = rank_F2 {ell(t) : q(t) != 0}.
```

The coordinate representatives `r_t` may be doubled roots, as in the replay.
This changes no supports. Suppose nine linearly independent pieces span `T`
and `dim(T intersect C) >= 5`. Their weights cannot be bounded respectively by
either of these multisets:

```
3,4,4,6,6,6,6,6,6
2,5,5,5,6,6,6,6,6.
```

These are precisely the two remaining `(b,t)=(5,4)` TWOSIDE beta shapes
reported by [PR3162](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3162). The new theorem excludes them directly, without a
space-pair or deletion-set census. Combining it with that predecessor's
thirteen exclusions removes its fifteen-shape residue. That combination
inherits the predecessor's finite theorem and TWOSIDE reduction. Neither
full C5, the other beta cells, `C(P112)>=64`, supplier admission nor kappa
is established here.

## Geometry used, with bounded replay

The replay reconstructs the 120 E8 root lines and removes the eight pinned
frame lines. All 960 simple reflections preserve the root inventory.
Simple-root coordinates modulo two, with a leading one, give
the nine-bit labels. Their bytes agree with the declared main-branch input.
All 3,309,747 four-dimensional annihilators and all 788,035 three-dimensional
annihilators in `F2^9` are enumerated in unique reverse row-echelon form.
Their kernels establish the sharp support capacities `g(5)=12`, `g(6)=20`.
For `d=2,3,4`, the leading-one coordinate gives the elementary upper bound
`g(d)<=2^(d-1)`, hence capacities `2,4,8`. A lower-dimensional support extends
to a flat of the stated dimension, so upper bounds on piece weights suffice.

Every nonzero codeword has support at least 53. Moreover, a codeword with
support below 70 is proportional to an E8 root codeword. Here is the
Weyl-chamber argument, with its finite quantities checked by the replay.
Below 70 means at least 43 live root lines are perpendicular. In a closed
Weyl chamber, perpendicular roots are generated by vanishing simple roots.
All 28 choices of six simple nodes contain at most 36 root lines. Thus
at least seven simple roots vanish. The eight seven-node faces have root-line
counts `42,28,22,14,16,23,37,63`. Only the last can reach 43; its normal is
a root direction. Weyl transformations preserve roots. Root directions have
live support 53 for 112 lines, or 56 for the eight removed frame lines.
This also proves the distance 53, since any putative smaller support would
be a root direction. The standard finite-root-system Weyl-chamber theorem
is used here, not formally proved by the executable.

This argument extends to `K`. The rational roots perpendicular to a nonzero
field-valued direction have rational rank at most seven. If that rank were
at most six, a generic real normal to their span would have exactly the
roots in that span perpendicular, contradicting the rank-six bound of 36.
Thus the rank is seven, the rational kernel is one-dimensional, and the
direction is proportional over `K` to its rational generator. Apply the real
argument to that generator. The P112 roots span eight dimensions, so the
map `h -> c_h` is injective.

## From nine pieces to six affine vertices

Split the basis into three small pieces `s_1,s_2,s_3` and six remaining
pieces `q_0,...,q_5`. Put `S=union supp(s_j)`, `s=|S|`, and
`U=sum_i |supp(q_i)|`. In the first shape choose small weights `3,4,4`;
in the second choose `2,5,5`.

Write `D=T intersect C` and let `lambda:T -> T/D`. Since `dim T=9` and
`dim D>=5`, the quotient has dimension at most four. For either split,
`S` together with the support of any one `q_i` has fewer than 53 lines.
The corresponding four quotient images are independent. Otherwise a
nonzero combination of four independent pieces would be a nonzero
codeword supported on fewer than 53 lines. Hence `dim(T/D)=4`, and the
three small quotient images are independent.

Modulo their span, all six images of the `q_i` are nonzero in a
one-dimensional space. Rescale each `q_i` to give them the same image.
Supports and independence are preserved. There are unique small-piece
combinations `a_i` such that

```
c_i = q_i - q_0 - a_i belongs to D,   i=1,...,5.
```

Set `c_0=0` and `a_0=0`. The five `c_i` are independent, by their distinct unit
coefficients on the nonbasis pieces `q_1,...,q_5`. Every edge

```
c_i-c_j = q_i-q_j-(a_i-a_j)
```

is nonzero and supported on `S union supp(q_i) union supp(q_j)`.
The support caps are at most 60 for the first shape and 66 for the second.
They are below 70, so all fifteen edges are root directions. By injectivity,
there are five independent vectors `h_i` with `c_i=c_{h_i}`, and each
nonzero difference among `0,h_1,...,h_5` is a scalar root.

## Root-simplex lemma

Normalize the real E8 roots to norm squared two. For two distinct root
lines, the only possible third root line in their rational plane occurs
in an A2 subsystem. It is represented by `alpha +/- beta` with coefficients
of absolute value one. The replay checks all 7,140 root-line pairs against
all 120 root lines using exact Gram determinants. It finds 3,780 planes
with two root lines and 3,360 with three. Alternatively this is the usual
rank-two simply-laced root-system fact.

This fact applies to a plane over `K` as well: any rational root in the
`K`-span of two independent rational roots is already in their rational
span, by solving a nonsingular rational two-by-two coordinate minor.

Write `h_i=b_i alpha_i`. Independence makes every pair of `alpha_i`
nonparallel. Since `h_i-h_j` is a third root line, the plane fact gives
`b_i/b_j=+1` or `-1`. Absorb these signs into the oriented roots. Thus
`h_i=b alpha_i` for one `b!=0`. Applying the same plane fact to their
differences gives `<alpha_i,alpha_j>=1` and makes each
`alpha_i-alpha_j` an actual norm-two root. The six vertices
`0,alpha_1,...,alpha_5` form a root A5 simplex.

Fix any E8 root `r` and evaluate it on those vertices. The six values

```
v = (0, <r,alpha_1>, ..., <r,alpha_5>)
```

are integers. Every difference is the inner product of two roots, hence
lies in `{-2,-1,0,1,2}`. If some difference has absolute value two,
equality in Cauchy-Schwarz makes `r` the corresponding oriented edge root.
The six values then have multiplicities `1,1,4`, giving nine unequal pairs.
If no difference has absolute value two, all values occupy at most two
consecutive integer levels. There are at most `3*3=9` unequal pairs again.
Thus every live coordinate belongs to at most nine of the fifteen edge
supports. Multiplication by the common field scalar `b` changes no zeros.
This bound is universal; the literal A5 fixture in the replay is only a
sharp positive control, not a replacement for the argument.

## Count incidences and exclude both shapes

Each edge codeword has at least 53 nonzero coordinates. At most `9s` edge
incidences occur in `S`. Outside `S`, its coordinate is exactly
`q_i(t)-q_j(t)`. An unequal pair has a nonzero endpoint, and each nonzero
one of the six `q_i(t)` can meet only five pairs. Summing over coordinates,

```
15*53 - 9s <= outside edge incidences <= 5U.
```

The support capacities give the following contradictions. Upper bounds on
`s` decrease the left side and upper bounds on `U` increase the right side,
so overlaps or smaller actual supports only strengthen them.

| Nine-piece shape | Small pieces | s cap | U cap | Required inequality |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `3,4^2,6^6` | `3,4,4` | 20 | 120 | `615 <= 600` |
| `2,5^3,6^5` | `2,5,5` | 26 | 112 | `561 <= 560` |

The second exclusion has margin exactly one under these bounds. Increasing
its small-support allowance from 26 to 27 would remove this contradiction;
the boundary control deliberately checks that case. No hypothesis that
the common deletion union lies in a five-flat is used.

## Remaining obligations

The proof concerns these two nine-piece configurations under the stated
intersection hypothesis. It uses the standard Weyl-chamber theorem and
finite exact capacity checks. There is no proof-kernel verification or
independent human review. The separate PR3162 reductions, the original
TWOSIDE feasibility filters and all other conjectures in PR3154 remain
their own dependencies. A closed weight residue does not certify a
decoder floor, a complete multiplication theorem or an improved exponent.
